questions.question: The central problem of 'for whom to produce' in an economy is concerned with:
options: A) Determining the efficiency of production
C) Distribution of income among people
D) Deciding what goods to produce
questions.explanation: 'For whom to produce' is the problem of distribution — deciding how the national income is to be divided among different members of society.

questions.question: A consumer is in equilibrium when the marginal utility of a good is equal to:
options: A) Total utility of the good
C) Average utility of the good
questions.explanation: In the single commodity utility approach, a consumer is in equilibrium when MU = Price. If MU > P, the consumer buys more; if MU < P, the consumer buys less.

questions.question: An increase in the price of a complementary good will lead to:
options: A) Rightward shift in demand curve of the given good
B) Movement along the demand curve of the given good
D) Leftward shift in demand curve of the given good
questions.explanation: A rise in the price of a complementary good reduces its demand, which in turn reduces the demand for the given good, shifting the demand curve leftward.

questions.question: If the price of a good falls from Rs. 15 to Rs. 12, and quantity demanded rises from 100 units to 150 units, the price elasticity of demand (using percentage method) is:
questions.explanation: % change in Q = (50/100)×100 = 50%. % change in P = (3/15)×100 = 20%. Ed = 50/20 = 2.5. Wait, let me recalculate: ΔQ = 50, average Q = 125; ΔP = -3, average P = 13.5. Using midpoint: %ΔQ = 50/125 = 40%, %ΔP = 3/13.5 = 22.2%. Ed = 40/22.2 ≈ 1.8.

questions.question: A movement along the demand curve is caused by a change in:
options: A) Price of the good itself
questions.explanation: Movement along the demand curve (extension or contraction of demand) occurs due to a change in the price of the good itself, ceteris paribus.

questions.question: A consumer has an income of Rs. 60 to spend on two goods X and Y priced at Rs. 6 and Rs. 4 respectively. The slope of the budget line (X on horizontal axis) is:
questions.explanation: Slope of budget line = -Px/Py = -6/4 = -3/2 = -1.5.

questions.question: In the short run, a production function shows the relationship between:
options: D) Fixed costs and variable costs
questions.explanation: The short run production function shows how output changes when variable inputs are changed, with fixed inputs held constant.

questions.question: When marginal product is falling but still positive, total product is:
options: D) Rising at a decreasing rate
questions.explanation: When MP is positive but falling, TP rises but at a decreasing rate. TP only falls when MP becomes negative.

questions.question: Which of the following cost curves is U-shaped?
questions.explanation: MC is U-shaped due to the law of variable proportions. AFC is a rectangular hyperbola, and TFC is a horizontal line.

questions.question: When average cost is falling, marginal cost must be:
questions.explanation: When AC is falling, MC < AC. MC pulls AC down when it is below AC, and pulls AC up when it is above AC.

questions.question: Under perfect competition, the average revenue of a firm is equal to:
questions.explanation: Under perfect competition, AR = MR = Price, since each unit is sold at the same market price.

questions.topic: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.question: Which of the following is a necessary condition for perfect competition?
options: B) Perfect knowledge among buyers and sellers
D) Few sellers and many buyers
questions.explanation: Perfect competition requires many buyers and sellers, homogeneous product, perfect knowledge, and free entry/exit.

questions.topic: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.question: A firm maximizes profit when:
options: C) MC = MR and MC is falling
D) MC = MR and MC is rising
questions.explanation: Profit maximization condition is MC = MR, with the additional requirement that MC must be rising (or cut MR from below) at that point.

questions.topic: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.question: The supply curve of a firm in perfect competition in the short run is the:
options: B) Average cost curve above AC
D) Marginal cost curve above AVC
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, the firm's short-run supply curve is the portion of the MC curve that lies above the minimum AVC (shut-down point).

questions.question: When the market price is below the equilibrium price, there is:
questions.explanation: At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, creating excess demand (shortage), which pushes the price upward.

questions.question: If the supply curve passes through the origin, the price elasticity of supply is:
questions.explanation: For a straight-line supply curve passing through the origin, elasticity = 1 (unitary elastic), since the ratio of percentage changes in Q and P is equal.

questions.question: The value added method of calculating national income avoids the problem of:
questions.explanation: The value-added method sums up the value added at each stage of production, thereby avoiding double counting of intermediate goods.

questions.question: Net National Product at factor cost (\( \text{NNP}_{FC} \)) is also known as:
questions.explanation: Net National Product at factor cost (NNP_FC) is the standard definition of National Income of a nation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of using GDP as a measure of welfare?
options: A) Income distribution is not captured
C) Government services are not counted
D) Environmental degradation costs are excluded
questions.explanation: Government services ARE counted in GDP (at cost). The other three are genuine limitations of GDP as a welfare measure.

questions.question: Money serves as a store of value because:
options: B) It is issued by the government
C) It is a medium of exchange
D) Its value remains stable over time
questions.explanation: Money can be saved and used for future purchases. For it to serve as a store of value, its purchasing power must remain reasonably stable.

questions.question: Which of the following is the lender of last resort?
questions.explanation: The RBI acts as lender of last resort, providing emergency funds to commercial banks facing liquidity crises.

questions.sub_topic: Policy Tools to Control Money Supply
questions.question: To reduce the money supply during inflation, the RBI will:
options: A) Buy government securities in open market
questions.explanation: Raising the CRR reduces the amount available for lending, contracting the money supply. This is a contractionary monetary policy measure.

questions.question: The four components of aggregate demand in an open economy are:
questions.explanation: AD = C (consumption) + I (investment) + G (government spending) + NX (net exports = X-M).

questions.question: Deficient demand leads to:
questions.explanation: When AD < AS at full employment, there is a deflationary gap, leading to involuntary unemployment and unused capacity.

questions.question: To correct deficient demand, the government should:
questions.explanation: Increasing government spending raises aggregate demand directly, helping to close the deflationary gap and reduce unemployment.

questions.question: If the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is 0.75, the investment multiplier is:
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/(1-MPC) = 1/(1-0.75) = 1/0.25 = 4. A Rs. 1 increase in investment raises income by Rs. 4.

questions.question: Tax receipts by the government are classified as:
questions.explanation: Tax receipts are revenue receipts because they neither create a liability nor reduce an asset. They are regular income for the government.

questions.question: Fiscal deficit is equal to:
options: A) Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts
B) Primary deficit minus interest payments
C) Total borrowing of the government
D) Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowing
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt creating capital receipts). It equals the borrowing requirement of the government.

questions.question: When government revenue receipts exceed its total expenditure, the budget is called:
questions.explanation: A surplus budget occurs when revenue receipts are greater than total expenditure, indicating net savings by the government.

questions.question: Which of the following is recorded in the capital account of the Balance of Payments?
questions.explanation: FDI is a capital account transaction (financial flows). Exports/imports of goods and services, and remittances, are current account items.

questions.question: Managed floating refers to an exchange rate system where:
options: A) The central bank intervenes to influence the rate while allowing market determination
B) The rate is completely fixed by the central bank
C) The rate is determined solely by market forces
D) Multiple exchange rates exist for different transactions
questions.explanation: Managed floating combines market determination with selective central bank intervention to prevent excessive volatility. India follows this system.

questions.sub_topic: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
questions.question: At the time of independence, India's economy was primarily:
questions.explanation: At independence, around 70% of the workforce was engaged in agriculture, and the industrial sector was underdeveloped due to colonial exploitation.

questions.question: The four common goals of India's Five Year Plans were growth, modernization, self-reliance, and:
questions.explanation: The common goals of India's planning were: growth (increase in GDP), modernization (adoption of new technology), self-reliance (reducing imports), and equity (reducing inequality).

questions.question: The Green Revolution in India introduced high-yielding varieties of seeds in:
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution was introduced in India around 1966-67, starting with high-yielding varieties of wheat in Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 divided industries into:
questions.explanation: IPR 1956 divided industries into three schedules: Schedule A (state monopoly), Schedule B (state-led development), and Schedule C (private sector).

questions.question: The New Economic Policy of 1991 introduced liberalisation by:
options: C) Removing industrial licensing for most industries
questions.explanation: Liberalisation in 1991 abolished industrial licensing (except for a few industries), reduced trade barriers, and opened sectors to private and foreign investment.

questions.question: Globalisation refers to:
options: B) Integration of national economies with the world economy
questions.explanation: Globalisation is the process of integrating the domestic economy with the world economy through trade, investment, and technology flows.

questions.question: A major criticism of the LPG reforms in India is that they led to:
options: A) Increased employment in all sectors
B) Growth without adequate employment generation (jobless growth)
C) Reduced regional and income inequalities
D) Decline in foreign exchange reserves
questions.explanation: Despite high GDP growth post-1991, employment growth remained sluggish. This 'jobless growth' is a major criticism of the LPG reforms.

questions.question: Human capital refers to:
options: D) The stock of skills and knowledge embodied in the population
questions.explanation: Human capital is the collective stock of skills, knowledge, and experience of the population that contributes to economic productivity.

questions.question: As per recent data, the Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) in higher education in India is approximately:
questions.explanation: India's GER in higher education (ages 18-23) is around 28%, reflecting both growth and the large population base.

questions.question: The informal sector in India is characterized by:
options: A) Lack of job security, no formal contracts, and no social security
C) Written contracts and social security benefits
D) High job security and regulated working hours
questions.explanation: The informal sector is characterized by small-scale operations, lack of formal contracts, no social security benefits, and irregular employment.

questions.question: A declining workforce participation rate in India, particularly among women, indicates:
options: A) A booming economy creating more jobs
B) Higher enrollment in education or discouraged worker effect
D) Improved labor laws protecting workers
questions.explanation: Declining female WPR reflects the 'discouraged worker effect' (people leaving the workforce) or higher enrollment in education, not necessarily economic prosperity.

questions.question: Among India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, which country has shown the most improvement in HDI ranking in recent years?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh has made remarkable progress in HDI, often ranking higher than India in recent years due to improvements in health, education, and gender parity.

questions.question: Compared to India, China's economy is more:
questions.explanation: China's development strategy focused heavily on manufacturing (export-led growth), making it the 'world's factory'. India's growth is more services-led.

questions.question: Both India and Pakistan have a similar population size, but Pakistan's per capita GDP (nominal) is lower than India's. A key reason for this divergence since the 1990s is:
options: D) India's higher investment in education and infrastructure, and service-led growth
questions.explanation: India's growth, driven by the IT services sector and higher investment in human and physical capital, outpaced Pakistan's, which faced political instability and lower development spending.

questions.question: Sustainable development means development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of:
options: B) Future generations to meet their own needs
D) The government to collect taxes
questions.explanation: The Brundtland Commission definition: sustainable development meets present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.

questions.question: India ranks among the top countries in the world in terms of:
options: C) Renewable energy capacity (solar and wind)
questions.explanation: India is among the top 5 countries globally in installed renewable energy capacity, with significant growth in solar and wind energy.

questions.question: In the two commodity case, a consumer is in equilibrium when:
questions.explanation: In the two commodity case, the law of equi-marginal utility states that equilibrium is reached when MUx/Px = MUy/Py, meaning the marginal utility per rupee spent is equal across both goods.

questions.sub_topic: Effect of Simultaneous Shift in Demand and Supply
questions.question: If both demand and supply of a good increase by the same proportion, the equilibrium:
options: B) Price remains unchanged, quantity rises
D) Price remains unchanged, quantity falls
questions.explanation: When both demand and supply increase by the same proportion, the equilibrium quantity rises, but the equilibrium price remains unchanged.

questions.question: The paradox of thrift suggests that:
options: A) If everyone tries to save more during a recession, aggregate saving may actually fall
B) Saving is always beneficial for economic growth
C) Higher savings lead to higher investment automatically
D) Thrift is a virtue that should be encouraged during booms
questions.explanation: The paradox of thrift, proposed by Keynes, states that during a recession, if everyone increases savings, aggregate demand falls, leading to lower income and ultimately lower total saving.
